item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking neural networks are neural networks that communicate with spikes: brief, discrete events that happen at particular moments in time.

item.title: Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Learners will understand why spiking neural networks use event-driven spikes, how their neuron and architecture ideas work, how they are trained, and how to evaluate tradeoffs among accuracy, latency, energy, spike count, and convergence for deployment choices.

item.title: 1. Why SNNs Need Events
item.description: 1. Why SNNs Need Events Build up why snns need events one step at a time.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a small robot watching a hallway through a camera while waiting for someone to walk by.

item.title: 1.2 Sparse Event-Driven Computation
item.description: Sparse Event-Driven Computation You already have the pieces for an event-based picture: information can arrive as discrete spike events, a spike train records those events over time, and dense computation keeps updating many values whether the input changed or stayed quiet.

item.title: 1.3 Temporal Dynamics in Spiking Computation
item.description: Temporal Dynamics in Spiking Computation Imagine a small gesture sensor watching a hand move through the air.

item.title: 1.4 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron Imagine a stream of spike events arriving at a neuron one time step after another.

item.title: 1.5 Lateral Inhibition in Spiking Architectures
item.description: A single spiking neuron can already turn accumulated input into an event: when its internal voltage reaches a firing threshold, it emits a spike.
